title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling for legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing incorrectly carries the client-side licensing list over to service-side auto-labeling; the current documentation explicitly directs administrators to a separate entitlement matrix. Its comparison with the Worldwide release also gives an outdated target month.

claims.quote: Microsoft Purview server-side auto-labeling will support legacy Microsoft Office file formats, including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt service-side auto-labeling change.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling legacy .doc .xls .ppt enable default rollout licensing meter; read the auto-labeling article and troubleshooting search excerpts. The article lists .docx, .pptx, .xlsx and PDF, not the legacy formats.

claims.claim: The auto-labeling article lists Word .docx, PowerPoint .pptx, Excel .xlsx and PDF as supported SharePoint and OneDrive formats.
claims.quote: PDF documents and Office files for Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), and Excel (.xlsx) are supported.

claims.claim: How existing policies will treat legacy formats when the extension arrives is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 578872 legacy Office auto-labeling default rollout enable GCC; Purview auto-labeling legacy .doc .xls .ppt enable default rollout licensing meter. Read the auto-labeling article and Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy reference; neither describes this extension's treatment of existing policies.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The arrival default of the legacy-format extension is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: 578872 legacy Office auto-labeling default rollout enable GCC. Read the roadmap description, auto-labeling article and policy reference. General policy defaults are documented, but no text states what this legacy-format extension does on arrival.

claims.claim: No admin switch is documented for the legacy-format extension.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling legacy Office files admin switch file extension Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy. Read the auto-labeling article and policy reference; searched the reference for legacy, extension, format, .doc, .xls and .ppt. Found policy controls, not a legacy-format switch.
claims.fix: Replace 'no admin switch is documented' with 'no admin switch specific to legacy-format support is documented' so the summary does not imply that the documented policy controls are absent.

claims.quote: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until they're deleted.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy reaches policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy ... When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -Mode Enable enables policy actions.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify. ... The Mode parameter specifies the action and notification level of the auto-labeling policy. ... Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: TestWithoutNotifications is the policy test mode.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations where you want to apply the label reaches policy location configuration.
claims.quote: For a policy in the Off section, select the Edit policy button. ... For the page Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -AddSharePointLocation "<site URL>" adds an included SharePoint location.
claims.quote: The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the SharePointLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: AddOneDriveLocation is the corresponding parameter for adding OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.
